title: Feasibility and acceptability of oral cholera vaccine mass vaccination campaign in response to an outbreak and floods in Malawi.
ehr_evidence: This study made use of the available health facility data and reports on cholera outbreak and oral cholera vaccine campaign. Data from OCV registers and tally sheets were summarized on daily summary sheets. Data from daily summary sheets were entered and analyzed in Microsoft excel.
summary: A documentation/feasibility study of the first large-scale reactive oral cholera vaccine (OCV) mass vaccination campaign targeting over 160,000 people aged one year and older in 19 internally displaced people camps and surrounding communities in Nsanje district, Malawi, reporting administrative coverage, demographic characteristics, and safety.
key_findings: First round coverage was 156,592 (97.6%) of 160,482 target population; second round coverage was 137,629 (85.8%).
Of 320,000 OCV doses received, 294,221 (91.9%) were administered, with 108,247 (67.6%) receiving the second dose.
Among 134,836 people with known gender and sex, 54.4% were females and 55.4% were children under 15 years of age.
No severe adverse event following immunization was reported.
The 2014/2015 outbreak produced 693 cases and 11 deaths (case fatality rate 1.6%, attack rate 0.013%).
captured_features: OCV administrative coverage by round and health facility catchment area
Number of doses administered (first and second dose)
Age and gender distribution of vaccinated individuals
Number of cholera cases and deaths by district and week
study_design: Documentation of a reactive mass vaccination campaign (descriptive feasibility/acceptability study)
population: Over 160,000 people aged one year and older living in 19 camps of internally displaced people and surrounding communities in Nsanje district, Malawi
limitations: Facility-based data subject to incompleteness and bias, with information obtained only from people who attended health facilities.
Information could not be obtained from non-vaccinated individuals.
No comparison group to assess vaccine effectiveness.
